title: Opportunity Velocity & Elasticity Map for Token-Constrained Roadmaps
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: Create a practical prioritization rubric that extends RICE to explicitly account for token budget constraints and latency sensitivity across customer cohorts. The Opportunity Velocity & Elasticity Map (OVEM) will be a dataset + scoring tool that helps PMs and GTM prioritize features and initiatives by expected net utility per token while preserving latency SLOs for sensitive customers.
background: Existing RICE variants at Redwood capture reach and impact, but teams report recurring trade-offs: features with modest reach but low token cost get deprioritized vs. high-reach, token-heavy work; conversely latency-sensitive fixes with small user coverage get buried. OVEM is motivated by three operational requirements: 1) make token cost explicit in prioritization, 2) factor in workload elasticity (how quickly cost scales with traffic and length), and 3) penalize latency regressions differently for SLO-bound cohorts. This complements the work in PM-54127 and the cost dashboards in console-2025.02.
scoring_algorithm: OVEM score = (Opportunity * VelocityMultiplier * ExperienceFactor) / (TokenElasticity * LatencyPenalty + BaselineCost). Definitions: Opportunity = estimated weekly active users impacted * avg value-per-user (USD) converted to internal utility points; VelocityMultiplier = expected delivery speed factor (1.0 = baseline, >1 if fast); ExperienceFactor = qualitative multiplier for strategic alignment (0.5-1.5); TokenElasticity = measured tokens per request growth factor (1.0 = linear, >1 if superlinear with length/feature); LatencyPenalty = cohort-weighted penalty (0-2) where >1 penalizes SLO breaches; BaselineCost = normalized token cost per-week scaled to utility units. The algorithm is intentionally unit-agnostic; PMs calibrate conversion factors using historical cost dashboards. The tool will surface both raw OVEM score and component breakdowns so teams can understand levers.
sample_calculation: Example: feature A affects 10k weekly users, estimated value-per-user = $0.20 -> Opportunity = 2000 utility pts. VelocityMultiplier = 1.2 (small scoped), ExperienceFactor = 1.0. TokenElasticity = 1.5 (feature increases average tokens per request by 50% under peak), LatencyPenalty = 1.1 (some SLO-sensitive cohorts affected), BaselineCost = 300 utility pts. OVEM = (2000 * 1.2 * 1.0) / (1.5 * 1.1 + 300/2000) ≈ (2400) / (1.65 + 0.15) = 2400 / 1.8 = 1333. Component view: net-utility-before-cost=2400, token-driven cost-multiplier=1.65, baseline-cost-abs=300 -> final score 1333. Use-case: prefer features with higher OVEM per estimated engineering-week when comparing across candidates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A reproducible scoring spreadsheet and Jupyter notebook implementing OVEM; 2) Integration prototype that reads per-route token profiles and latency cohort weights from console dashboards; 3) A sample prioritized list of 12 initiatives (mixed quick wins + strategic bets) using OVEM, with a short rationale for top 6; 4) Review and sign-off from Eng (runtime), Observability, and Growth PMs; 5) Documentation page in Confluence describing calibration steps and limitations.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): build spreadsheet + notebook; sample data from console dev region; internal demo with PM guild. Phase 2 (3 weeks): engineering hooks for auto-populating tokenElasticity and latency cohorts from the Console API; create a lightweight OVEM tab in the existing prioritization template. Phase 3 (2 weeks): run a 'shadow prioritization' for next quarter roadmap; collect feedback and retrain conversion factors. Phase 4 (ongoing): adopt OVEM as optional lens in quarterly kickoff and in executive prioritization reviews.
stakeholders: Product: Asha Menon (owner), Diego Alvarez (assignee). Engineering: Priya Rao (runtime), Marcus Liu (observability). Design: Nora Patel (PM tooling UX). Growth/Revenue: Elena Kim. Finance: Omar Diaz (cost calibration). Exec review: VP Product (TBD).
risks: 1) Converting USD value-per-user to utility points is subjective and may bias towards revenue-facing work. 2) TokenElasticity estimates can be noisy for new features—risk of over-penalizing creative features. 3) LatencyPenalty requires reliable cohort tagging in telemetry; gaps in instrumentation will reduce accuracy. Mitigations: use conservative priors, require sensitivity analysis, and flag high-uncertainty scores.
dependencies_notes: Needs Console API endpoints for per-route token histograms (ENG-4021) and cohort latency SLIs (ENG-1842). Also requires a Confluence page template (PM-PRD) and security sign-off if sensitive customer telemetry is surfaced (security_review_required = false for initial prototype).
